assertion_analysis.failure_condition: test_an_unsplittable_command_has_no_action_form (tests/test_an_unsplittable_command_has_no_action_form.py:130-136) asserts pytest.raises(ValueError, match='No closing quotation') on the stdlib split and then action_form(command) is None. Reinstating the unguarded shlex.split (the regression) makes action_form raise the ValueError out of the test, so the assertion reddens; the negative-control.log records exactly this case failing.

test_the_obligations_read_completes_over_the_stored_command (:150-166) drives the production composer through obligations() over a fixture review and asserts the row survives with next_command and no next_action_form. With the guard removed, obligations() raises ValueError before returning, so the test errors; negative-control.log records it failing. The expected text comes from a test-side re-derivation (_stored_command) of the composer's own f-string, but it is not a value fed into the code under test — the composer derives its text from the fixture review — so the assertion is independent of the value it checks.

test_a_splittable_command_still_has_an_action_form (:139-144) is a positive control asserting action_form('reckon crew complete --run r-x --gate pass') equals the literal 'crew(action="complete", run_id="r-x", gate="pass")'; it would redden if the guard overreached and also suppressed well-formed commands.
